To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of MTHFR polymorphisms and twin gestations could be a risk factor for cerebral stroke in children.

1) MTHFR C 677 T polymorphism is not a major cause of stroke in pediatric patients; 2) in twin pregnancy with fetal demise, a careful thrombophilia work-up is needed to prevent recurrence of thrombotics events; 3) a folate supplementation is needed in women with MTHFR C667T homozygous and in twin pregnancies with fetal demise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of a correct thrombophilia work-up in twin pregnancies, in which the presence of genetic polymorphism could increase the risk of fetal and perinatral cerebral stroke.
the possible role of MTHFR polymorphisms as a risk factor in the development of fetal stroke in twin gestation.
the possible relationship between MTHFR gene polymorphism and fetal/perinatal cerebral stroke.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

MTHFR gene polymorphisms could be considered as a potential risk for cerebral stroke and that folate supplementation could be a useful tool to prevent cerebral damage in twin pregnancies with co-twin death.
the MTHFR polymorphism is not the only cause of stroke, and that other genetic factors and/or other environmental factors should be considered.
a genetic thrombophilia screening should be performed in all twin pregnancies and, above all in twin pregnancies in which one twin died before the 24th week of gestation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MTHFR polymorphisms are not a risk factor for cerebral stroke, but they could be a predisposing factor for thrombotic events in a multifactorial context.
the presence of MTHFR polymorphism, associated with a twin gestation with a co-twin demise, could increase the risk of cerebral stroke in the survivor.
a genetic screening in the presence of twin pregnancy is mandatory to avoid severe fetal and peripartum brain damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of MTHFR C/T or MTHFR A/A polymorphism could be considered as a risk factor for the development of cerebral stroke in twin gestation.
the genetic predisposition to thrombosis, in particular the homozygosity of MTHFR C667T, could be associated to fetal/perinat stroke in twin gestation.
the presence of MTHFR polymorphism could increase the risk of stroke in children with a twin gestation with the demise of the co-twin in utero.
